newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO CORN FUTURES CLOSE MOSTLY UP, SPOT SEPT DOWN.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO CORN FUTURES CLOSE MOSTLY UP, SPOT SEPT DOWN.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended mostly higher on Thursday, as the market remained bullish after gains on the previous day, traders said.
The spot September contract, which expires on Friday, ended down 350 yen at 15,570. Open interest in the contract was 4,917 lots as of August 13.
Other prices were 60 to 180 yen higher at the close, with benchmark July 1998 up 180 yen at 14,810 yen per tonne.

"There was still a bullish mood. Some local investors continued to buy," a brokerage house trader said. The Tokyo corn market surged on Wednesday, after the CBOT market posted sharp gains due to the USDA's bullish 1997 U.S. corn output estimates.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system stood at $2.62-1/4 per bushel at 0705 GMT, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.75 per bushel at 0705 GMT, against $7.79 at Wednesday's close.
